title: Inside stays in, return comes out
idea: TOOL. Predict what a function shares (return) versus what stays private (inside variables). Reinforces scope with visible output.

exercises.prompt:
Read:

def score():
    points = 10
    return points

print(score())
exercises.explanation: score makes points = 10 and returns it. The returned 10 is printed.
With no return, score hands back None. The private points is never shared, so print shows None.

exercises.prompt:
Which line will cause an error?

def f():
    x = 5
    return x

print(f())
print(x)
options: print(x) — x is private to f
exercises.explanation: f() works and returns 5. But print(x) outside fails: x only exists inside f.

exercises.prompt: Two functions can each have their own variable called total without interfering.
exercises.explanation: Yes — each function's total is private. That is exactly why scope is useful.

exercises.prompt:
Predict:

def a():
    n = 1
    return n

def b():
    n = 100
    return n

print(a() + b())
exercises.explanation: a()'s n is 1, b()'s n is 100 — separate private notes. 1 + 100 = 101.

exercises.prompt: Arrange a correct program: define double, return its result, then print the call.
exercises.explanation: Make a private result, return it, print the returned value: 12.

exercises.prompt: Why can't you write print(result) after calling double(6)?
exercises.explanation: result lives only inside double. Outside, the name is unknown.

exercises.prompt:
Hand the private total back out of the function:

def sum_two(a, b):
    total = a + b
    ____ total
exercises.explanation: return total shares the value. Without it, total stays trapped inside.

exercises.prompt: A function printed the right answer but you can't use it later. Likely fix?
options: Return the value instead of (or as well as) printing it
exercises.explanation: print only shows it on screen; return hands it back so other code can use it.

exercises.prompt: Reaching into a function's private variable from outside is a common beginner mistake.
exercises.explanation: Very common — the fix is always to return the value you want to use.
